processes.name: Salary structures & market pricing
processes.summary: Maintains the global salary structure (job-based ranges by job family, level and geo zone) and reprices it every year against semiconductor-specific survey data such as Radford/Aon, with local cuts for Bengaluru, Taipei/Hsinchu and Shanghai/Shenzhen. Scope covers benchmark matching, range and geo-differential construction, the good-faith posting ranges that pay-transparency laws require, and loading ranges to Darwinbox and Greenhouse. Good looks like ranges refreshed before the annual review opens, defensible match quality, and posting ranges that match what the company actually pays.
processes.owner: Total Rewards (process and ranges), HR Analytics (survey data), Legal (pay-transparency and antitrust review)
processes.trigger: Annual survey release on the comp calendar (typically Q3, ahead of annual review budgeting), or a new job family, new location or material market movement for a critical skill
outputs: Benchmark match file with survey source and match quality for each job
Salary range tables by job family, level and geo zone, in local currency
Geo differential table and zone assignment by work location
Posting-range table for each pay-transparency jurisdiction
CHRO-approved range change memo with cost and below-minimum impact
Updated range tables in Darwinbox and Greenhouse
processes.sla: Annual refresh approved and loaded 6 weeks before annual review planning opens; new-job pricing within 10 business days of request

steps.label: Launch annual market pricing cycle
steps.detail: Confirm survey participation and deadlines (e.g., Radford/Aon semiconductor cut for US and Canada, plus local technology cuts for India, Taiwan and China) and the market reference policy (e.g., P50 base, P60-P75 for critical design skills). Fix the range effective date to match the annual review calendar.

steps.label: Submit and validate survey census
steps.detail: Extract job, level, location and pay from Darwinbox as of the survey effective date, map to survey job codes and submit only through the survey vendor. Send China employee data de-identified or with PIPL notice and separate consent for the cross-border transfer (verify with privacy counsel).

steps.label: Match benchmark jobs and age data
steps.detail: Match at least 60-70% of employees to benchmark jobs, record match quality (exact, close or blended), and age survey data to the common effective date using projected movement. Blend sources where a single survey has thin samples, e.g., analog/mixed-signal, RF or DFT roles.

steps.label: Build ranges and geo differentials
steps.detail: Set midpoints from the market reference, apply level-based spreads (e.g., 40% for early-career, 60% for senior levels) and geo zones by work location in local currency. Check range minimums against legal floors: California exempt salary ($70,304 in 2026, $72,384 in 2027; $122,573.13 for salaried computer professionals in 2026) and local minimum wages for support and intern roles.

steps.label: Review impact with HRBPs
steps.detail: HRBPs review who would fall below the new minimums, compression between levels and between managers and reports, and cost by org. Below-minimum cases are routed to the annual review (CO-02) or to CO-05 market adjustments.

steps.label: Review posting ranges and data use
steps.detail: Legal confirms posting ranges are the good-faith range the company expects to pay at hire (not the full structural range) for each pay-transparency jurisdiction. It also confirms benchmarking used only vendor-aggregated data and no direct wage exchanges with competitors (wage-fixing has been a criminal offence in Canada since June 2023).
steps.control: Legal sign-off on posting-range table before load

steps.label: Approve range changes?
steps.detail: The CHRO approves range movement, the cost of lifting employees to new minimums and the posting ranges. If movement exceeds budget tolerance, the CHRO may phase increases over two cycles.

steps.label: Load ranges to Darwinbox and ATS
steps.detail: Load approved tables with the agreed effective date to Darwinbox and Greenhouse. A second person compares loaded values to the approved file before release.
steps.control: Dual review of loaded range tables against the approved file

steps.label: Publish ranges and guidance
steps.detail: Publish ranges to recruiters, HRBPs and managers with role-based access. Give employees a documented way to request the pay scale for their own role where law requires it (e.g., California).

controls.control: Posting ranges reviewed against the approved structure and each jurisdiction's rules before they reach Greenhouse
controls.evidence: Legal sign-off on the posting-range table

controls.control: Loaded range tables compared with the CHRO-approved file by a second reviewer
controls.evidence: Load comparison report with reviewer sign-off

controls.control: Market data obtained only through third-party survey vendors; no direct exchange of pay plans with competitors
controls.evidence: Survey participation log and Legal-approved benchmarking protocol

kpis.name: Benchmark coverage
kpis.target: >= 65% of employees matched to a benchmark job with documented match quality
kpis.why: Thin matching makes ranges hard to defend in pay-equity and transparency challenges

kpis.name: Offers within range
kpis.target: >= 95% of offers inside the approved range
kpis.why: Offers outside range signal stale ranges or weak governance and undercut good-faith posting claims

kpis.name: Range currency
kpis.target: 100% of ranges refreshed within 12 months
kpis.why: Design-skill markets move fast; stale ranges drive failed offers and counteroffers

considerations: Price roles by skill family, not title: analog/mixed-signal, RF, physical design, DFT and verification often need a premium or separate range from generic 'hardware engineer' benchmarks.

Keep the structural range and the posting range separate. The posting range must be what you reasonably expect to pay at hire (California SB 642); the structural range can be wider to cover long-tenured employees.
Geo zones follow work location, not HQ. A remote engineer in Colorado or Washington brings that state's pay-transparency rules even if the manager sits in San Jose.
Treat survey submissions as antitrust-sensitive: use third-party vendors with aged, aggregated data and never share current or future pay plans with competitors.
Refresh range minimums every January for legal floors (California exempt threshold, local minimum wages) even in years when the market refresh is light.

variations.when: New job family or location (e.g., opening a Hsinchu validation lab)
variations.how: Price ad hoc within 10 business days using the closest benchmark and local survey cut; the CHRO approves an interim range until the next annual refresh.

variations.when: Mid-year market spike for a named skill
variations.how: Total Rewards issues a temporary market premium for that skill with CHRO approval and reviews it at the next refresh instead of moving the whole structure.
Map acquired jobs to the job architecture (PL-03), then price and decide whether to red-circle, green-circle or phase employees to the new ranges over one to two cycles.

countries.us: Maintain good-faith posting ranges for every pay-transparency jurisdiction (CO, WA, NY, IL, MN, MD, HI, DC, NJ, VT, MA and CA, plus VA from Jul 1, 2026, ME from Jul 29, 2026 and CT from Oct 1, 2026) and treat 'remote - US' roles as covered. Keep exempt ranges above the federal $684/week floor and higher state thresholds.
countries.us-ca: Postings must show a good-faith estimate of the range the company reasonably expects to pay (SB 642, 15+ employees), employees may request the pay scale for their current role, and job title and wage history must be kept for employment plus 3 years. Set exempt range minimums at or above $70,304 (2026) / $72,384 (2027), and $122,573.13 for salaried computer professionals (2026).
countries.ca: Ontario postings (25+ employees, since Jan 1, 2026) need a pay figure or range no wider than C$50,000 (roles above C$200,000 exempt) and BC postings need the expected pay or range. Benchmarking must avoid direct competitor wage exchanges, which are criminal under the Competition Act since June 23, 2023.
countries.in: There is no posting-range mandate, but build ranges on CTC with basic + DA at 50% or more of remuneration (Code on Wages 'wages' rule, since 21 Nov 2025) or PF, gratuity and leave-encashment costs rise. Price VLSI, verification and physical design separately from generic IT because Bengaluru chip-design GCCs move faster.
countries.tw: Salary ranges must be posted only for roles paying under NT$40,000/month (Employment Services Act Art. 5), which rarely hits engineering roles. Price total cash including year-end bonus and profit-sharing months, because engineers compare against TSMC and MediaTek profit-sharing.
countries.cn: No posting-range requirement; price Shanghai and Shenzhen separately and model employer social insurance and housing fund on top of cash (Shanghai contribution base cap RMB 37,731 from 1 Jul 2026). Submit China census data to survey vendors de-identified or with PIPL notice and separate consent.

processes.name: Annual compensation review
processes.summary: Runs the annual merit, promotion and equity refresh cycle for all eligible employees, from budget setting with FP&A through manager planning in the comp tool, calibration, a privileged pay equity check before lock, approvals up to the CEO and Comp Committee, and a reconciled load to Darwinbox and payroll. It is one of the largest pay-change events of the year, so it is run with SOX-grade data controls. Good looks like spend within budget, clear pay-for-performance differentiation, no unexplained pay gaps, zero payroll load errors and letters delivered on time in every country.
processes.owner: Total Rewards (process), HRBP (manager enablement and calibration), FP&A (budget), Payroll (load and reconciliation); Comp Committee approves officer pay and the equity pool
processes.trigger: Annual comp calendar: budget approval in Q4, final performance ratings from PD-02, and country effective dates (e.g., 1 April for US, Canada and India)
outputs: Approved merit, promotion and equity refresh budgets by country and org
Guidelines matrix, eligibility rules and country effective-date calendar
Approved manager recommendations with justification for exceptions
Privileged pre-lock pay equity memo and adjustment log (held by Legal)
Comp Committee resolutions for officer pay and the refresh pool
Reconciled HRIS/payroll load and equity grant list; employee comp letters
processes.sla: About 12 weeks from budget approval to letters; pay changes reconciled on the first payroll after each country's effective date

steps.label: Set merit, promo and equity budgets
steps.detail: FP&A and Total Rewards set country merit budgets from survey salary-increase projections (India and China usually run above the US), a promotion pool and an equity refresh pool in shares and dollars within the burn-rate and share-reserve limits the Comp Committee approved. Budgets are built into the operating plan and accruals.

steps.label: Publish guidelines and eligibility
steps.detail: Build the merit matrix (rating x compa-ratio), promotion increase guidance, refresh grant guidelines by level and rating, and eligibility rules (hire-date cutoff, leaves, notice periods, recent off-cycle increases). Publish one calendar of country effective dates and payroll cut-offs.

steps.label: Extract and validate comp tool data
steps.detail: Snapshot Darwinbox (job, level, base, range, FTE, currency, manager hierarchy) and final ratings from the Performance module, then load the comp tool. Reconcile headcount and total base payroll by entity to the payroll register before opening the tool.
steps.control: SOX data extract integrity: IPE completeness and accuracy check; headcount and base payroll reconciled to payroll by entity, signed by preparer and independent reviewer

steps.label: Train managers and open planning
steps.detail: HRBPs brief managers on guidelines, pay-for-performance expectations, equal-pay rules and what may not be said before approval (no promises, no discussion of others' outcomes). Planning opens with a 2-3 week deadline.

steps.label: Plan merit, promotion and equity
steps.detail: Managers enter recommendations in the comp tool within budget and guidelines. Increases outside the matrix, zero increases for solid performers and promotions above guideline need a written justification; promotions must be approved through PD-04 or flagged for approval in the tool.

steps.label: Calibrate with dept heads
steps.detail: HRBPs and dept heads review each org's budget use, differentiation between rating groups, compa-ratio outliers, promotion consistency and retention of critical skills (e.g., analog, physical design, verification). Changes are made in the tool so the audit trail is kept.

steps.label: Run pre-lock pay equity check
steps.detail: At Legal's direction and under privilege, HR Analytics regresses proposed post-cycle pay (base, bonus target and refresh grant value) by gender globally and by race/ethnicity in the US, within job family, level and location. Unexplained gaps above threshold go back to HRBPs with suggested fixes funded from the cycle budget.
steps.control: Privileged pay equity review completed before lock; memo held by Legal

steps.label: Within budget and equity-clean?
steps.detail: Total Rewards confirms each org is within budget tolerance (e.g., +/-0.1 point of payroll), exceptions are justified and flagged gaps are fixed or documented. Orgs that fail go back to managers with specific fixes.

steps.label: Approve org totals and exceptions
steps.detail: The CEO, with the CHRO and CFO, approves org-level spend, above-guideline exceptions and VP-level outcomes, and recommends pay for Section 16 officers other than the CEO to the Comp Committee. The CEO takes no part in decisions on their own pay.

steps.label: Approve officer pay and equity pool
steps.detail: The Comp Committee approves Section 16 officer increases, bonus targets and refresh grants, the aggregate non-officer refresh pool and any delegation, and sets CEO pay in executive session without the CEO (Nasdaq 5605(d); see CO-07). Grants are made on the fixed grant date under EQ-01, never before approval.
steps.control: Committee minutes and resolutions; approved grant list signed before the grant date

steps.label: Lock cycle and generate load files
steps.detail: Lock the tool and generate the HRIS pay-change file (effective date, reason code, new range) and the approved refresh grant list for Stock Admin. Check each country's effective date against its payroll cut-off; where a load misses cut-off, schedule retro pay in the next regular payroll rather than off-cycle runs.

steps.label: Load and reconcile pay changes
steps.detail: People Ops loads the file to Darwinbox, which feeds the payroll provider. Payroll reconciles count, total dollar change and effective dates between the locked tool, Darwinbox and the first payroll register after the effective date; retro pay for non-exempt employees includes recalculated overtime.
steps.control: SOX: locked tool = Darwinbox = payroll register, independently reviewed; refresh grants reconciled approved list = equity platform = accounting

steps.label: Deliver conversations and letters
steps.detail: Managers hold conversations once letters are released in Darwinbox: new base, increase %, bonus target and any refresh grant ('subject to approval and grant on the scheduled date'). Country formats apply: India increment letter with revised CTC annexure, China bilingual salary adjustment notice acknowledged by the employee, Taiwan notice in Traditional Chinese.

steps.label: Close cycle and review outcomes
steps.detail: Report spend against budget, differentiation, promotion rates and post-cycle gap results to the CHRO and Comp Committee. Archive approvals, reconciliations and letters for SOX and records retention, and feed lessons into next year's guidelines.

raci.activity: Data extract and comp tool load
Officer pay and refresh pool approval

controls.control: Comp tool extract reconciled to Darwinbox and payroll (headcount and base payroll by entity) before planning opens
controls.evidence: Signed reconciliation and IPE query evidence

controls.control: Above-guideline and over-budget recommendations blocked without documented approval in the tool workflow
controls.evidence: Comp tool approval audit trail

controls.control: Privileged pay equity review of proposed outcomes before lock
controls.evidence: Counsel memo and adjustment log held by Legal

controls.control: Officer pay and the refresh pool approved by the Comp Committee before effective and grant dates; CEO absent for CEO pay
controls.evidence: Minutes and signed resolutions

controls.control: Locked tool = Darwinbox = payroll register (count, dollar change, effective date) after load
controls.evidence: Reconciliation workpaper signed by preparer and independent reviewer

controls.control: Refresh grants reconciled: approved list = equity platform = ASC 718 expense
controls.evidence: Three-way reconciliation per grant date

controls.control: Comp tool access limited by hierarchy; planners cannot load payroll
controls.evidence: Quarterly user-access review

kpis.name: Budget adherence
kpis.target: Spend within +/-0.2 point of approved budget in every country
kpis.why: Overspend compounds into base payroll for years

kpis.name: Pay-for-performance differentiation
kpis.target: Top-rated employees receive >= 1.5x the average merit % of solid performers
kpis.why: Flat increases waste budget and lose top engineers

kpis.name: Load accuracy
kpis.target: Zero pay changes needing off-cycle correction
kpis.why: Errors mean off-cycle payments, SOX exceptions and lost trust

kpis.name: Letters on time
kpis.target: 100% of letters released within 10 business days of lock and before the effective-date payroll
kpis.why: Late letters undercut the message and, in India, the April payroll

kpis.name: Post-cycle pay equity
kpis.target: No cohort with a statistically significant unexplained gap after lock
kpis.why: Fixing gaps inside the cycle is cheaper than separate remediation

considerations: Choose one or two global effective dates and document exceptions; India's April-March financial year makes 1 April natural, while Taiwan and China often tie raises to the year-end bonus and Lunar New Year period.
Set budgets by country from survey projections, not a global average; India and China salary movement usually exceeds the US and Canada.
Keep the matrix simple (rating x range position) and give managers discretion with justification; complex matrices get gamed.
Run the pay equity check before lock so fixes come out of the merit budget; keep it privileged (HR Analytics works at counsel's direction) and never circulate raw regression outputs.
Include equity refresh and bonus targets in the equity check: California now treats stock, options and bonuses as wages under the Equal Pay Act.
Avoid retro pay where possible by setting effective dates after the load; retro increases for non-exempt staff require overtime recalculation.
Treat the comp tool as a SOX system: auditors test completeness of the population and the reconciliation to payroll, so keep IPE evidence.
Moving China employee data into a US-hosted comp tool needs PIPL notice and separate consent; limit visibility by hierarchy for all countries.
Use refresh grants deliberately for critical design talent; in 2027 very large grants to non-officers can also bring engineers into the expanded 162(m) group.

variations.how: Handled through PD-04 and CO-05; employees promoted within a set window before lock (e.g., 3 months) get merit only on the new base.
Excluded from merit (or prorated per guidelines) and reviewed at the next cycle; still eligible for a refresh grant if the offer said so.
Remains eligible and is reviewed on pre-leave performance; do not exclude or reduce because of leave (e.g., FMLA/CFRA, Taiwan parental leave, China maternity).

variations.when: Employee under notice or on a PIP
variations.how: Increase deferred or excluded per guidelines; in China and Taiwan no pay reduction without written agreement.

variations.when: Pay freeze or reduced budget year
variations.how: Zero or reduced merit with focus on equity refresh and below-minimum fixes; India CTC restructuring for the 50% wages rule still proceeds.
Follow CO-07: Comp Committee approval, CEO pay set in executive session, and CD&A disclosure.
Separate budget and a lagged cycle until mapped to job architecture and ranges.

countries.us: Retroactive increases for non-exempt employees must be applied to overtime hours in the retro period at the new regular rate. Keep exempt salaries above the federal $684/week floor and higher state thresholds, and apply the employee's work-state rules for remote staff, including posting ranges on internal promotion notices in pay-transparency states.
countries.us-ca: SB 642 counts bonuses, stock/options and benefits as wages under the Equal Pay Act (sex, race, ethnicity), with a 3-year limitation period and recovery back up to 6 years, so the pre-lock check must cover bonus targets and refresh grants, not base alone. Non-exempt employees need written notice of a pay-rate change within 7 calendar days unless it appears on the next wage statement (LC 2810.5). Exempt pay must meet $72,384 (2027) and the DIR computer-professional rate each 1 January.
countries.ca: Ontario employers with 10+ employees must maintain pay equity between female and male job classes (Pay Equity Act), so recheck job-class rates after the cycle. BC employers with 50+ employees publish gender pay-gap reports (first due Nov 1, 2026, covering hourly pay, overtime and bonus gaps), so cycle outcomes flow into the next report. Pay reductions or restructuring risk constructive dismissal and need written agreement.
countries.in: The cycle follows the April-March financial year: issue increment letters with a revised CTC annexure effective 1 April so April pay (due before 7 May) carries the change. Use the cycle to keep basic + DA at 50% or more of remuneration (Code on Wages 'wages' rule, since 21 Nov 2025) and collect new-regime tax elections. Code on Wages s.3 bars gender discrimination in pay.
countries.tw: Engineers compare total cash (12 months' base plus year-end bonus and profit-sharing months) with TSMC and MediaTek, so guidelines should show total-cash impact. Year-end bonuses are paid before Lunar New Year, and raises are commonly aligned to January or the post-Lunar New Year period (market practice, verify local benchmark). Update Labor Insurance, NHI and pension insured salary grades after increases (verify filing timing).
countries.cn: Raises are commonly effective in January or April, with year-end bonuses paid before Spring Festival (market practice). Any reduction or structural change needs written agreement (LCL Art. 35) or supports an Art. 38 resignation with severance. Social insurance and housing fund bases reset each July on prior-year average wage (Shanghai from 1 Jul 2026: RMB 7,546-37,731).

processes.name: Annual bonus / variable pay
processes.summary: Governs the company-wide annual cash bonus plan for non-sales employees: metric and funding design, quarterly accrual, year-end funding certification, individual allocation, payout and leaver rules by country. Executive officer payouts are certified by the Comp Committee and stay subject to the clawback policy. Good looks like a formula employees understand, accruals that true up within tolerance, on-time payouts in every country and leaver rules that hold up under local law.
processes.owner: Total Rewards (design and calculation), Finance (accrual and funding certification), Comp Committee (plan approval and officer payouts)
processes.trigger: Comp Committee approval of the fiscal-year plan; quarterly close for accruals; fiscal year-end results for payout
outputs: Plan document with country addenda and leaver rules
Quarterly bonus accrual memo and journal support
Certified funding calculation tied to audited results
Comp Committee certification minutes for officer payouts
Approved individual payout file
Payout reconciliation to each country's payroll register
processes.sla: Funding certified within 45 days of fiscal year-end; global plan paid by March 15 of the following year (US short-term deferral), with local customary year-end bonuses paid before Lunar New Year

steps.label: Approve plan metrics and targets
steps.detail: The committee approves funding metrics (e.g., revenue and non-GAAP operating margin, optionally a product milestone such as tape-outs or design wins), threshold/target/maximum curves (e.g., 50/100/200%) and the individual modifier range. Metrics must not be demographic-linked; APAC leadership may carry an export-compliance modifier.

steps.label: Publish plan document and addenda
steps.detail: Publish the plan with eligibility, proration, leaver rules, discretion and clawback language, plus country addenda (Canada notice-period wording, China adoption through democratic procedure, Taiwan LSA Art. 29 interplay). Communicate individual targets in Darwinbox and capture acknowledgments.

steps.label: Accrue bonus quarterly
steps.detail: Accrue each quarter on forecast attainment and eligible headcount; the Controller reviews assumptions and true-ups.
steps.control: Quarterly accrual review by the Controller with documented assumptions

steps.label: Certify year-end funding
steps.detail: Calculate funding from audited results with an independent recalculation, apply only committee-approved adjustments with documented rationale, and issue the funding certificate.
steps.control: Independent recalculation tied to audited results before certification

steps.label: Certify results and officer payouts
steps.detail: The committee certifies funding and approves executive officer payouts. Calculation records are kept at least three years because payouts tied to financial measures fall under the Rule 10D-1 clawback.

steps.label: Allocate individual awards
steps.detail: Managers allocate within the funded pool in the comp tool using final PD-02 ratings and the modifier range; zero awards for eligible employees need a documented reason.

steps.label: Pool balanced and eligibility clean?
steps.detail: Total Rewards checks pool balance by org and applies eligibility rules for new hires, leaves (protected leave cannot be penalized beyond what law permits), transfers and leavers by country.

steps.label: Pay and reconcile by country
steps.detail: Pay through each country payroll: US supplemental withholding (22%, 37% above $1M), Taiwan 2.11% NHI supplementary premium above 4x monthly insured salary, and China separate annual-bonus taxation where better for the employee. Reconcile the approved file to each payroll register.
steps.control: Approved payout file = payroll register by country, independently reviewed

steps.label: Archive records and review plan
steps.detail: Archive calculations, approvals and reconciliations for at least three years, and review the funding curve, differentiation and employee understanding before next year's design.

controls.control: Funding calculation independently recomputed and tied to audited results before committee certification
controls.evidence: Signed calculation and committee minutes

controls.control: Quarterly accrual reviewed against forecast attainment
controls.evidence: Accrual memo and journal entry support

controls.control: Approved payout file reconciled to each payroll register
controls.evidence: Payout reconciliation with reviewer sign-off

kpis.name: Payout accuracy
kpis.target: >= 99.9% of payments correct first time
kpis.why: Corrections create off-cycle cost and erode trust

kpis.name: Accrual true-up
kpis.target: Year-end true-up within 5% of accrued amount
kpis.why: Large true-ups signal weak forecasting and draw audit attention

kpis.name: Differentiation
kpis.target: Top-rated employees receive >= 1.5x the average payout % of solid performers
kpis.why: Undifferentiated bonuses do not retain top talent

kpis.name: On-time payment
kpis.target: 100% paid by each country's payout date
kpis.why: Late payment breaches local wage timing and US short-term deferral

considerations: Label the plan carefully: a formula-driven bonus is non-discretionary, so it enters the overtime regular rate for US non-exempt staff and vacationable wages in Canada.

Draft leaver rules country by country. 'Employed on payment date' works in much of the US, but Canadian plans must expressly exclude the common-law notice period, and China and Taiwan leaver rules need local review (verify).
Avoid double-dipping in Taiwan and China, where customary year-end bonuses (13th month) coexist with the global plan; state which payment satisfies LSA Art. 29 or local contract promises.
Keep financial-measure calculations audit-ready: any officer payout based on revenue, margin or TSR is recoverable after a restatement, so the recalculation must be reproducible three years later.
Do not tie bonuses to demographic outcomes; DOJ's 2026 IBM False Claims Act settlement cited demographic-linked bonuses.

variations.how: Prorate from start date; hires after the eligibility cutoff (e.g., 1 October) join next year's plan.

variations.when: Transfer between countries or plans mid-year
variations.how: Prorate by days in each plan and pay in the currency of the employing country at payout; Payroll reviews tax sourcing.

variations.when: Leaver by RIF, retirement or death
variations.how: Pay prorated target or actual per plan and separation terms (OF-03, OF-08, OF-09); voluntary leavers and for-cause terminations follow country addenda.
Prorate only where law permits and never lower the individual modifier because of the leave.

countries.us: A formula bonus is non-discretionary, so for non-exempt employees it must be allocated back into the overtime regular rate for the periods earned (29 CFR 778); federal supplemental withholding is 22% (37% above $1M). Whether an 'employed on payment date' condition defeats a leaver's claim depends on state wage law and plan wording (verify by state).
countries.us-ca: Non-discretionary bonuses feed the daily-overtime regular rate and, from 2026, count as wages under the Equal Pay Act (SB 642). Earned bonuses are due with final pay, and AB 692 limits clauses requiring repayment of bonuses at departure outside the standalone discretionary-bonus exception.
countries.ca: Common-law notice damages include the bonus that would have been earned during the notice period unless plan wording unambiguously removes it (Matthews v. Ocean Nutrition, 2020 SCC 26). Non-discretionary bonuses are vacationable wages for 4%/6% vacation pay.
countries.in: The statutory bonus (8.33%-20% for employees earning up to INR 21,000/month, paid by 30 Nov) is separate from the performance bonus and mainly affects support roles. The performance bonus is taxed as salary with TDS under s.392 of the Income-tax Act 2025.
countries.tw: LSA Art. 29 requires a bonus or profit share for fault-free employees in a profit year, and the Taiwan entity's articles must set an employee-compensation percentage of profit decided by the board (Company Act Art. 235-1). Pay before Lunar New Year and withhold the 2.11% NHI supplementary premium on bonuses above 4x the monthly insured salary.
countries.cn: Bonus rules bind leavers only if adopted through democratic procedure and publicized, and courts may award a pro-rata year-end bonus to employees who left after the performance year (verify local case law). The annual one-off bonus can be taxed separately from monthly salary once a year through 31 Dec 2027, and bonuses count in the 12-month average wage used for economic compensation.

processes.name: Sales incentive compensation
processes.summary: Designs, documents and pays incentive compensation for sales, field applications engineers and business development staff selling chips and IP to OEM/ODM customers. Covers plan documents with signed acknowledgments, quota and crediting rules, SPIFF approval, an export-compliance gate on order credit, calculation, ASC 340-40 capitalization, disputes and leavers. Good looks like every plan signed before the first payout, accurate statements, and no commission ever paid on an order that failed screening.
processes.owner: Total Rewards - Sales Compensation (design and administration), Sales leadership (quotas), Finance (calculation review and accounting), Trade Compliance (order gate)
processes.trigger: Fiscal-year plan launch; hire, promotion or transfer into an incentive role; monthly or quarterly commission close
outputs: Plan document and individual quota/target letters
Signed plan acknowledgments (e-signature records)
SPIFF approvals with written terms
Commission statements and calculation workpapers
ASC 340-40 capitalization and amortization schedule
Dispute log with decisions
processes.sla: Plans signed within 30 days of fiscal-year start or role change; commissions paid within 30 days of period close; disputes resolved within 15 business days

steps.label: Design plan, quotas and crediting
steps.detail: With Sales leadership and Finance, set pay mix (e.g., 50/50 for account managers, 70/30 or 80/20 for FAEs), measures (bookings, revenue, design wins), accelerators, caps, draws and crediting for multi-region customers (design-win site versus ship-to). Include recovery of commissions on cancelled or returned orders.

steps.label: Issue plan and target letters
steps.detail: Send each participant the plan document and individual target letter through e-signature, stating how commissions are computed, when they are earned and paid, and treatment on termination.

steps.label: Sign plan acknowledgment
steps.detail: Participants sign and receive a signed copy. Unsigned participants are escalated to their manager and no payout is released until signature.
steps.control: No payout released without a signed acknowledgment on file

steps.label: Request SPIFFs within governance
steps.detail: In-year SPIFFs need written terms and pre-approval by the Sales VP, Total Rewards and Finance before launch. No SPIFFs to distributor or customer employees without Legal anti-bribery review.
steps.control: SPIFF pre-approval record before launch

steps.label: Clear orders before credit
steps.detail: Orders earn credit only after restricted-party screening and any required export license clear. Orders on hold or later found non-compliant are excluded or clawed back.
steps.control: Crediting blocked for orders without screening-cleared status

steps.label: Calculate, accrue and capitalize
steps.detail: Calculate commissions from booked and billed data, accrue expense, and capitalize incremental costs of obtaining contracts under ASC 340-40 with amortization over the benefit period. An independent reviewer checks the calculation before statements go out.
steps.control: Independent review of calculations and the ASC 340-40 schedule (SOX)

steps.label: Statement disputed?
steps.detail: Participants review statements and may dispute crediting or calculation within the plan window (e.g., 30 days).

steps.label: Resolve dispute and document
steps.detail: Sales Comp investigates with Sales Ops and Finance, decides under plan terms and records the outcome in the dispute log. Exceptions need Sales VP and Total Rewards approval.

steps.label: Pay commissions and reconcile
steps.detail: Pay through payroll on the plan date, including earned commissions in final pay for leavers by local deadlines, and reconcile the approved file to the payroll register.

steps.label: Close period and analyze plan
steps.detail: Archive statements and approvals and track cost of sales, attainment distribution and windfall deals for plan redesign.

controls.control: Signed plan acknowledgment on file before any payout
controls.evidence: E-signature records matched to payout file

controls.control: Order credit only after export screening and license clearance
controls.evidence: Crediting system hold report and Trade Compliance clearance log

controls.control: Independent review of commission calculations and ASC 340-40 capitalization
controls.evidence: Reviewer sign-off and capitalization reconciliation

controls.control: SPIFFs launched only with written terms and pre-approval
controls.evidence: SPIFF approval records

kpis.name: Plans signed on time
kpis.target: 100% signed within 30 days of FY start or role change
kpis.why: Unsigned plans breach California and New York rules and weaken the company's position in disputes

kpis.name: Calculation accuracy
kpis.target: < 1% of payout value adjusted after statements are issued
kpis.why: Errors are the main source of disputes and wage claims

kpis.name: Dispute resolution
kpis.target: 90% resolved within 15 business days
kpis.why: Slow resolution distracts sellers and escalates to claims

considerations: Semiconductor sales cycles are long (design win to production revenue often takes 12-36 months), so blend revenue credit with design-win milestones or the plan pays people who have left and nothing to those who won the socket.
Define exactly when a commission is earned (booking, shipment or cash): that choice decides what must go in final pay in California and other states.

Treat export controls as a comp design issue: regulators credit plans that deny credit for unscreened orders and claw back pay for violations, as the Cadence (2025) and Applied Materials (2026) cases showed.
SPIFFs paid to non-exempt inside sales staff enter the overtime regular rate; SPIFFs to channel partners are an anti-corruption risk.
Changes to earning events or clawback terms change the ASC 340-40 capitalization; involve Finance before plan changes.

variations.when: Mid-year hire, promotion or territory change
variations.how: Issue a new target letter and signed acknowledgment; prorate quota and use split-credit rules for transferred accounts.
Pay commissions earned under plan terms by the local final-pay deadline; unearned pipeline follows the plan, and Canadian notice-period treatment is reviewed.
If the signed plan has a windfall clause, deals above a threshold (e.g., 150% of annual quota) are reviewed by the Sales VP and Total Rewards before crediting.

countries.us: Several states require written, signed commission agreements covering earning, draws and post-termination payment (e.g., NY Labor Law 191(1)(c), MN), and unclear plans risk multiple damages under state wage laws. Commissions paid to non-exempt staff are part of the regular rate.
countries.us-ca: LC 2751 requires a written commission contract stating how commissions are computed and paid, with a signed copy to the employee and a signed receipt returned. Earned commissions are due immediately on discharge or within 72 hours of resignation without notice, with waiting-time penalties of up to 30 days' wages (LC 203).
countries.ca: Commissions are vacationable wages for 4%/6% vacation pay, and common-law notice damages include commissions that would have been earned during the notice period unless the plan clearly excludes them.
countries.in: Commission is excluded from 'wages' for PF and gratuity but counts toward the 50% exclusion cap, and recovering overpaid commission through payroll is limited to authorised deductions within the 50% cap (Code on Wages s.18).
countries.tw: Regular sales incentives are likely 'wages' under the LSA, raising the average wage used for severance and pension (verify), and overpayments cannot be pre-deducted from wages without agreement (LSA Art. 22, 26).
countries.cn: Commission rules must be adopted through democratic procedure and publicized to bind employees, and payroll deductions to recover losses are capped at 20% of monthly wage. Hold credit on China-customer orders until export screening clears; the Cadence plea involved China-subsidiary sales staff selling to an Entity-Listed university.

processes.name: Off-cycle adjustments & counteroffers
processes.summary: Handles pay changes outside the annual review: market and internal-equity adjustments, counteroffers to employees who resign or are at high flight risk, and targeted retention awards for critical skills. It balances speed (a counteroffer made after the employee has mentally left is wasted) with budget, pay-equity and approval control. Good looks like decisions within two business days, no new unexplained gaps and tracked retention outcomes.
processes.owner: HRBP (process and flight-risk judgement), Total Rewards (pricing), Dept Head and CHRO (approval authority)
processes.trigger: Resignation with a competing offer, documented flight risk for critical talent, an employee below range minimum, or an internal-equity issue raised by a manager, HRBP or pay equity audit
outputs: Request with justification and competing-offer summary
Range and peer-equity analysis
Approval record under the authority matrix
Counteroffer or adjustment letter, plus retention award agreement if used
Pay change in Darwinbox and equity request to Stock Admin
Retention outcome log at 6 and 12 months
processes.sla: Counteroffer decision within 2 business days of resignation; other off-cycle adjustments within 10 business days

steps.label: Request adjustment or counteroffer
steps.detail: The manager submits the request in Darwinbox with reason code, current and proposed pay, and for counteroffers the competing role and package as described by the employee (do not require a copy of the offer letter).

steps.label: Assess criticality and flight risk
steps.detail: The HRBP assesses performance, scarcity of the skill (e.g., analog, SerDes, physical design), succession cover and whether pay is really the driver, using a stay conversation. Resignations to PRC-linked or direct competitors are flagged to Security under the trade-secret protocol.

steps.label: Counteroffer or adjust?
steps.detail: Proceed only for regrettable losses or documented pay issues where pay is a real driver; otherwise the resignation proceeds under OF-01.

steps.label: Price against range and peers
steps.detail: Check compa-ratio, range position and pay of peers in the same job, level and location so the change does not create a new unexplained gap. Prefer time-vested RSUs or deferred cash over large base jumps and fund from the off-cycle pool (e.g., 0.5% of payroll).
steps.control: Peer-equity check before approval

steps.label: Approve within authority
steps.detail: The dept head approves within budget; increases above range maximum or above a threshold (e.g., 15%) go to the CHRO, and Section 16 officers go to the Comp Committee (CO-07).
steps.control: Approval matrix enforced in the Darwinbox workflow

steps.label: Deliver offer and document
steps.detail: The manager delivers the counteroffer or adjustment with a written letter. Retention awards use forward-vesting terms and no repayment clause that local law prohibits; equity is stated as subject to approval and the scheduled grant date.

steps.label: Process pay and equity changes
steps.detail: People Ops loads the change in Darwinbox for the next payroll cut-off and sends any equity request to Stock Admin under EQ-01; Payroll confirms the change on the register.

steps.label: Track retention at 6 and 12 months
steps.detail: The HRBP records whether the employee stayed at 6 and 12 months and shares results with Total Rewards to test whether ranges or refresh guidelines need to change.

steps.label: Close request; route to offboarding
steps.detail: If no counteroffer is made, the HRBP closes the request and starts OF-01, including the departing-employee trade-secret protocol.

controls.control: Off-cycle changes approved according to the authority matrix before load
controls.evidence: Darwinbox workflow approval trail

controls.control: Peer-equity comparison documented before approval
controls.evidence: Pricing worksheet attached to the request

controls.control: Quarterly review of off-cycle spend, approvals and retention outcomes against budget
controls.evidence: Quarterly off-cycle report reviewed by Total Rewards and FP&A

kpis.name: Decision speed
kpis.target: 90% of counteroffer decisions within 2 business days
kpis.why: Counteroffers made late rarely work

kpis.name: 12-month retention of countered employees
kpis.why: Shows whether counteroffers buy real retention or only delay exits

kpis.name: Off-cycle spend
kpis.target: Within the approved pool (e.g., 0.5% of payroll)
kpis.why: Uncontrolled off-cycle spend undermines the annual review

considerations: Counteroffers reward resigning; set criteria (regrettable, critical skill, pay is the driver) so managers do not use them as a routine raise route.
Anchor the new pay on the range and peer comparison, not the other company's number; in California, voluntarily disclosed pay history cannot justify a pay gap.

Prefer forward-vesting RSUs or deferred cash over upfront bonuses with repayment clauses: California AB 692 restricts stay-or-pay terms and India enforces clawbacks only as reasonable liquidated damages.
Watch compression: one engineer jumped above peers triggers a queue of requests, so fix the range or peer group at the same time where needed.

variations.how: Comp Committee approval (CO-07); a material new arrangement may require an 8-K Item 5.02(e) within four business days.

variations.when: Group retention (M&A, RIF survivors, critical tape-out program)
variations.how: Run as a program with a pooled budget, standard retention agreement and CHRO approval instead of one-off requests.
Adjustments identified in CO-06 follow its privileged process and are loaded through this workflow with a neutral reason code.

countries.us: Mid-period increases for non-exempt employees must be prorated and any retro overtime recalculated. Retention bonuses with repayment terms need state-law review because many states restrict deductions to recover them (e.g., NY Labor Law 193).
countries.us-ca: AB 692 bars requiring departing workers to repay retention and similar amounts under agreements from 1 Jan 2026, except discretionary upfront bonuses under standalone agreements; a bill presented 3 Sep 2026 would delay this to 1 Jan 2027 and extend the exception to retention bonuses (verify outcome). Document the range and peer basis for the new pay, since voluntarily disclosed pay history cannot justify a gap.
countries.ca: Retention letters should confirm that the existing termination clause and equity terms continue to apply, because new terms without fresh consideration may be unenforceable. BC prohibits reprisal for discussing pay, so assume counteroffer terms will circulate.
countries.in: Counteroffers are routine in Bengaluru design centers with 60-90 day notice periods; retention clawbacks are enforceable only as reasonable, pro-rated liquidated damages and payroll recovery is capped at 50% of wages. Keep revised CTC at 50%+ basic + DA.
countries.tw: Flag resignations of core engineers to PRC-linked employers to Security given MJIB poaching investigations (17 firms questioned in Jul-Aug 2026). Update Labor Insurance, NHI and pension insured salary after increases (verify timing).
countries.cn: Raises are easy but later reductions need written consent (LCL Art. 35), so put retention money in a separate conditional bonus rather than base. Higher pay also raises any post-employment non-compete compensation, which is set as a share of prior 12-month average pay.

processes.name: Pay equity audit & remediation
processes.summary: Annual privileged statistical audit of base, bonus and equity pay by gender globally and by race/ethnicity in the US, directed by counsel, with root-cause review, a remediation budget and adjustments. It also lines up with statutory reporting (California pay data, BC pay transparency report, Ontario pay equity). Good looks like no statistically significant unexplained gap in any major cohort, remediation effective before the annual review locks, and root causes fixed upstream in offers and promotions.
processes.owner: Legal (privilege, scope and advice), HR Analytics (analysis), Total Rewards (remediation), CHRO (budget approval)
processes.trigger: Annual calendar (Q3, before annual review budgeting), acquisition integration, a pay complaint or claim, or a statutory report deadline
outputs: Counsel engagement letter and privileged scope memo
Privileged regression results and outlier list
Root-cause findings (starting pay, promotion timing, acquisitions)
Approved remediation list and budget
Adjustments loaded in Darwinbox with neutral reason codes
Non-privileged summary for leadership and statutory reports
processes.sla: Analysis to remediation load within 12 weeks; adjustments effective before the annual review lock

steps.label: Engage counsel and set scope
steps.detail: Counsel commissions the audit in writing to give legal advice, defines populations, pay elements and groups, and limits distribution. Statutory reports are prepared in a separate, non-privileged workstream.

steps.label: Build dataset and comparator groups
steps.detail: Assemble base, target and actual bonus, equity grant value and benefits where material, plus legitimate factors (job family, level, location, tenure, time in level). Group employees doing substantially similar work, not just the same title.

steps.label: Run regressions and outlier review
steps.detail: Run multivariate regressions by gender (all countries) and race/ethnicity (US), test significance by cohort, and list individuals well below predicted pay (e.g., residual below -5%). Label results privileged and share only with counsel and named reviewers.
steps.control: Privileged labeling and restricted access list

steps.label: Investigate root causes with counsel
steps.detail: At counsel's direction, HRBPs review flagged cases for legitimate explanations (performance, recent hire, acquisition) and systemic causes such as starting pay, promotion timing or retention grants.

steps.label: Unexplained gap to remediate?
steps.detail: Counsel advises which cohorts and individuals need adjustment, considering statistical and legal significance.

steps.label: Size remediation and budget
steps.detail: Calculate individual adjustments to predicted pay or peer median, model California back-pay exposure over the look-back window, and prepare the budget request.

steps.label: Approve remediation budget
steps.detail: The CHRO (with the CFO if outside the merit budget) approves the budget and timing. Adjustments are made whether or not employees have asked.

steps.label: Load adjustments
steps.detail: People Ops loads adjustments with a neutral reason code and effective date, Payroll reconciles the approved list to the register, and letters use counsel-approved wording.
steps.control: Approved remediation list = Darwinbox = payroll register

steps.label: Fix root causes and report
steps.detail: Update offer approval, promotion and refresh guidelines to address root causes, feed non-privileged results into required reports (BC report, California pay data), and re-test flagged individuals next year.

controls.control: Analysis commissioned by counsel with privileged labeling and restricted access
controls.evidence: Engagement letter and access list

controls.control: Approved remediation list reconciled to Darwinbox and payroll
controls.evidence: Signed reconciliation

controls.control: Prior-year flagged individuals and new-hire offers re-tested each year
controls.evidence: Privileged re-test results held by Legal

kpis.name: Unexplained gap
kpis.target: No cohort with a statistically significant unexplained gap; adjusted gender gap under 1%
kpis.why: The core measure of pay-equity risk

kpis.name: Remediation completion
kpis.target: 100% of approved adjustments effective before the annual review lock
kpis.why: Late fixes get diluted by merit increases

kpis.name: Recurrence
kpis.target: < 10% of remediated individuals flagged again the next year
kpis.why: Recurrence means root causes are not fixed

considerations: Privilege is fragile: the analysis must be requested by counsel for legal advice with limited circulation; do not paste regression outputs into leadership decks or statutory reports.
Include every pay element counted as wages: after SB 642, a clean base-pay model with skewed equity refresh grants still leaves California exposure.
Performance ratings used as a control variable can hide bias; test rating distributions by group before accepting them as an explanation.
Starting pay is the usual root cause; fix it upstream in TA-04 offer approval (range-based offers, no salary history questions).

Remediate individuals based on the analysis rather than running demographic-targeted pay programs; after Ames and the DOJ Civil Rights Fraud Initiative, programs must be open to all and tied to identified gaps.

variations.how: Run a pre-close or day-100 analysis of the acquired population and budget integration adjustments separately.
Route through ER-02 with Legal, run a targeted privileged analysis of the comparator group and consider a legal hold (ER-09).

variations.when: Statutory report year (BC by Nov 1; California in May)
variations.how: Reconcile report job groupings with audit cohorts so published gaps can be explained, without disclosing the privileged analysis.

countries.us: The federal Equal Pay Act covers equal work, while states such as NY, MA, IL, CO, WA, NJ, MD and OR use 'substantially similar' or broader comparators; Illinois requires an Equal Pay Registration Certificate at 100+ IL employees. Keep the audit privileged.
countries.us-ca: SB 642 extends the Equal Pay Act to 'another sex', race and ethnicity, counts bonuses, stock/options and benefits as wages, and allows recovery back up to 6 years within a 3-year limitation period, so size back-pay exposure over that window. The CRD pay data report (100+ employees; due 12 May 2027 with 23 SOC-based categories) is non-privileged and should reconcile to audit groupings.
countries.ca: Ontario's Pay Equity Act (10+ employees) requires maintaining pay equity between female and male job classes of equal or comparable value, alongside ESA s.42 equal pay. BC employers with 50+ employees must publish a gender pay-gap report by Nov 1, 2026 covering hourly pay, overtime and bonus gaps, and non-compliant employers may be publicly named.
countries.in: Code on Wages s.3 bars gender discrimination (including against transgender persons) in pay for the same or similar work; there is no reporting duty, but include Bengaluru in the global gender analysis.
countries.tw: The Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 10 requires equal pay for work of equal value, with complaints heard by local gender equality committees; there is no pay-gap reporting duty.
countries.cn: Equal pay for equal work (LCL Art. 63) and the Women's Rights Law (2022) apply. Moving employee-level pay and gender data to US analytics needs PIPL notice, separate consent and a cross-border transfer mechanism, so consider running the China cut locally or de-identified.

processes.name: Executive compensation cycle
processes.summary: The Comp Committee's annual cycle for Section 16 officers and NEOs: advisor independence, peer group and benchmarking, tally sheets, incentive and PSU design and certification, CEO and officer pay decisions, and proxy disclosure (CD&A, compensation tables, pay ratio, pay versus performance, say-on-pay). It also covers event-driven work: 8-K Item 5.02, 162(m) and 280G modeling, clawback readiness and Item 402(x) grant timing, while tracking the SEC's May 2026 disclosure proposal. Good looks like decisions that are minuted and defensible, filings on time, strong say-on-pay support and no comment letters.
processes.owner: Comp Committee (decisions), Total Rewards - Executive Compensation (process), Legal - Securities/Corporate Secretary (disclosure and filings), CHRO (management accountability)
processes.trigger: Comp Committee annual calendar tied to the fiscal year, plus events: officer hire, promotion or departure, change in control, or accounting restatement
outputs: Committee calendar, charter review and minutes
Advisor independence assessments
Peer group, benchmarking report and tally sheets
CEO and officer pay decisions with incentive and PSU certifications
Proxy (CD&A, compensation tables, pay ratio, pay versus performance) and 8-K Items 5.02 and 5.07
162(m) covered-employee list and 280G estimates
processes.sla: Proxy within 120 days of fiscal year-end; 8-K Items 5.02 and 5.07 within 4 business days; Form 4 within 2 business days of grants

steps.label: Adopt annual committee calendar
steps.detail: At the Q3 meeting the committee adopts next year's calendar: Q4 (peer group, incentive design, tally sheets), Q1 (certify results, set officer pay, grant on the fixed date), Q2 (proxy and say-on-pay), mid-year (burn rate, share reserve, 162(m) and 280G modeling). It also reviews its charter annually.

steps.label: Assess advisor independence
steps.detail: Before retaining or renewing the compensation consultant and outside counsel, the committee considers the six Rule 10C-1 / Nasdaq 5605(d) independence factors using annual questionnaires. Fees for other services above $120,000 and any conflicts are captured for Item 407(e)(3) disclosure.
steps.control: Six-factor questionnaires and minuted conclusion before engagement

steps.label: Refresh peer group and benchmarks
steps.detail: The independent consultant proposes a peer group of roughly 15-20 semiconductor and adjacent companies screened on revenue, market cap and talent overlap, reconciled to ISS-selected peers and the TSR peer group used for pay versus performance. It benchmarks base, target bonus, long-term incentives and total direct compensation for each officer role.

steps.label: Build tally sheets; model 162(m)/280G
steps.detail: Produce tally sheets per officer (realized and realizable pay, outstanding equity, severance and change-in-control walkaway), annual 280G estimates (3x base amount; best-net cutback preferred to gross-ups) and the 162(m) covered-employee list, including the five additional highest-paid employees for tax years after Dec 31, 2026.

steps.label: Design annual incentive and PSU metrics
steps.detail: With the consultant and Finance, propose annual bonus metrics (e.g., revenue, non-GAAP operating margin, strategic design-win or tape-out milestones) and PSU metrics (e.g., relative TSR against a semiconductor index plus a financial metric over three years) with threshold/target/maximum curves. The committee approves the design at its Q4 meeting; no demographic-linked metrics, and every financial measure is covered by the clawback policy.

steps.label: Compute results and PSU attainment
steps.detail: After fiscal year-end, Finance calculates bonus funding and PSU attainment from audited results and market TSR data, with an independent recalculation reviewed by Internal Audit. Workpapers are kept at least three years for Rule 10D-1 recovery.
steps.control: Independent recalculation before certification; workpapers retained 3+ years

steps.label: Recommend other officers' pay
steps.detail: The CEO presents performance assessments and pay recommendations for the other executive officers, using the benchmarks and tally sheets. The CEO leaves the meeting for any discussion of CEO pay.

steps.label: Certify results; set officer pay
steps.detail: The committee certifies incentive and PSU results, approves officer base, payouts, targets and LTI values, and sets CEO pay in executive session with the consultant but without the CEO (Nasdaq 5605(d)). Minutes record the rationale that will support the CD&A.
steps.control: CEO recusal minuted; signed certification resolution

steps.label: Approve grants on fixed grant date
steps.detail: Officer grants are approved on or before the scheduled grant date by the committee of non-employee directors (Rule 16b-3). NEO options are not granted from four business days before to one business day after a 10-Q, 10-K or MNPI 8-K (Item 402(x)), and the same calendar is applied to RSUs and PSUs.
steps.control: Grant calendar and Item 402(x) window check signed by Legal

steps.label: Record grants; feed Form 4 data
steps.detail: Stock Admin records grants in the equity platform the same day and sends grant and withholding data to Legal within one business day so Forms 4 are filed within two business days (EQ-05).

steps.label: File 8-K Item 5.02 when triggered
steps.detail: File within four business days of the decision (not the effective date) for officer appointments and departures, and for new or materially amended compensatory arrangements with the PEO, PFO or an NEO (5.02(e)) unless consistent with previously disclosed plans. Use Item 5.02(f) for salary or bonus omitted from the Summary Compensation Table once determined.

steps.label: Draft CD&A and compensation tables
steps.detail: With the consultant and Legal, draft the CD&A, Summary Compensation Table (3 years), grants of plan-based awards, outstanding equity, vested/exercised, termination and change-in-control payments, director pay, compensation-risk statement (402(s)), clawback (402(w)) and 402(x) narratives. Perquisites are tracked at aggregate incremental cost, disclosed at $10,000 or more, and itemized above the greater of $25,000 or 10% of total perks.
steps.control: Tables tied out to payroll, equity platform and ASC 718 values; Disclosure Committee review

steps.label: Compute pay ratio and pay vs performance
steps.detail: With Payroll and HR Analytics, identify the median employee from all worldwide employees (US, Canada, India, Taiwan, China) on a date in the last three months of the fiscal year using a consistently applied measure (re-usable up to three years; non-US de minimis exclusion up to 5%). Compute compensation actually paid for five years using year-end and vest-date fair values, and tag in Inline XBRL.

steps.label: File proxy; report vote on 8-K 5.07
steps.detail: File the DEF 14A within 120 days of fiscal year-end with say-on-pay (and frequency or equity plan proposals when due), then report vote results on 8-K Item 5.07 within four business days of the annual meeting.

steps.label: Say-on-pay support adequate?
steps.detail: The committee reviews support levels and investor and proxy-advisor feedback. Weak support (ISS scrutinizes below 70%, Glass Lewis below 80% - verify current thresholds) triggers off-season shareholder outreach with IR and Legal and a responsiveness section in the next CD&A.

steps.label: Close cycle; feed next-year design
steps.detail: Archive minutes, workpapers and filings, update the SEC-rule watchlist (including the May 2026 filer-status proposal) and roll lessons into the next committee calendar.

raci.activity: CD&A, tables, pay ratio and pay versus performance

controls.control: Six-factor independence assessment of consultant and counsel before engagement and annually
controls.evidence: Questionnaires and committee minutes

controls.control: CEO absent from deliberation and voting on CEO pay
controls.evidence: Executive-session minutes

controls.control: Incentive and PSU attainment independently recalculated before certification and kept 3+ years
controls.evidence: Calculation workpapers with Internal Audit review

controls.control: Officer grants approved on or before fixed grant dates and checked against Item 402(x) windows and blackouts
controls.evidence: Grant calendar, resolutions and Legal checklist

controls.control: Proxy compensation tables tied out to payroll, the equity platform and ASC 718 values
controls.evidence: Tie-out binder and Disclosure Committee sign-off

controls.control: HR notifies Legal the same day of officer appointments, promotions and departures
controls.evidence: Notification log matched to 8-K and Form 3 dates

controls.control: Perquisites tracked year-round at aggregate incremental cost
controls.evidence: Perquisite log reconciled to AP and payroll

kpis.name: Say-on-pay support
kpis.target: >= 90% (never below 70%)
kpis.why: Low support triggers proxy-advisor 'against' recommendations for committee members

kpis.name: Filing timeliness
kpis.target: 100% of proxy, 8-K and Form 4 filings on time
kpis.why: Late filings are disclosed and can cost S-3 eligibility

kpis.name: CEO pay positioning
kpis.target: Target total direct compensation within +/-15% of peer median unless the committee documents a reason
kpis.why: Keeps pay defensible to investors and proxy advisors

kpis.name: Disclosure quality
kpis.target: Zero SEC comment letters or corrections on compensation disclosure
kpis.why: Errors in compensation actually paid and tables are hard to correct publicly

kpis.name: Certification timeliness
kpis.target: Results certified within 60 days of fiscal year-end
kpis.why: Late certification delays payouts, grants and the proxy

considerations: The SEC's May 19, 2026 proposal (Rel. 33-11419) would keep full disclosure only for large accelerated filers with a public float of $2B or more; others would drop CD&A, pay ratio, pay versus performance and say-on-pay. Comments closed July 20, 2026 and adoption for the 2027 proxy season is unconfirmed (verify), so estimate the company's likely category, plan the 2027 proxy both ways and keep pay ratio and pay versus performance data processes running until a final rule.

Section 162(m) expands for tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2026: the five highest-paid employees beyond the named officers are added each year, and large RSU vests or sign-on awards to non-officer engineers can qualify. Model the lost deduction with Tax for the 2027 budget.
Public companies cannot use the shareholder cleansing vote for 280G, so rely on best-net cutbacks (ISS treats excise-tax gross-ups as problematic) and refresh estimates annually and before any deal.

Semiconductor results are cyclical; relative TSR against a semiconductor index plus a financial metric balances cycle noise, but pre-agree how TSR-based awards would be recalculated for clawback purposes.
Keep the talent peer group (who you hire from) and the performance peer group consistent or explain differences; pay versus performance TSR uses the disclosed peer group.
Track perquisites such as personal security and aircraft use year-round; the SEC chair has signaled perquisite reform, but current rules apply until changed.
Apply the Item 402(x) calendar to RSUs and PSUs too, and schedule off-cycle executive new-hire grants away from earnings and MNPI 8-Ks.
Do not use demographic-linked incentive metrics; they create legal risk after 2025-26 federal DEI enforcement.
Confirm every executive has signed the clawback acknowledgment and that offer letters, plans and severance agreements reference the policy filed as Exhibit 97.

variations.when: New executive officer hired from outside
variations.how: TA-09 offer approved by the committee; inducement grants under Nasdaq 5635(c)(4) need independent-director approval and a press release; 8-K Item 5.02 within four business days and Form 3 within 10 days.

8-K Item 5.02(b) within four business days of notice or decision; separation agreement drafted for public filing, with 409A six-month delay for specified employees and whistleblower carve-outs (OF-04).
Refresh 280G calculations, prepare the golden-parachute disclosure (Item 402(t)) and vote, and design retention consistent with CIC plans.
Trigger the clawback process (EQ-06) and recalculate affected incentive awards.
Committee-led shareholder outreach, documented changes and a responsiveness section in the next CD&A.

variations.when: Executive officer based outside the US
variations.how: Deliver pay through local payroll with tax equalization as needed; plan clawback collection within local wage-deduction limits; Section 16 reporting still applies.

variations.when: Final SEC rule adopted and company is a non-accelerated filer
variations.how: Switch to scaled disclosure only after the rule is effective, and decide with the committee which voluntary disclosures investors still expect.

countries.us: Full Item 402 disclosure (CD&A, tables, pay ratio, pay versus performance, 402(x)), annual say-on-pay with results on 8-K Item 5.07, and 8-K Item 5.02 for officer changes and material NEO arrangements, each within four business days. Section 162(m) caps the deduction at $1M per covered employee and adds five more employees from 2027; 280G applies a 20% excise tax and lost deduction at 3x the base amount; 409A requires a six-month delay on separation payments to specified employees. The May 2026 proposal would scale disclosure back if the public float is below $2B (verify final rule).
countries.us-ca: California executives cannot be bound by non-competes (B&P 16600, including agreements signed elsewhere), so condition severance and change-in-control benefits on releases, confidentiality and cooperation rather than non-competition. AB 692 limits repayment demands at separation beyond the mandated clawback, and SB 642's equal-pay rules cover executives' bonus and equity as wages.
countries.ca: For any Canada-based executive officer, bonus and equity forfeiture wording must expressly exclude the common-law notice period (Matthews), which can reach about 24 months for senior leaders. Canadian employees are in the pay-ratio population, and equity income is reported on the T4.
countries.in: Indian employees are part of the worldwide pay-ratio population (unless within the up-to-5% non-US de minimis exclusion), with payroll data pulled from the Indian entity as of the determination date. Any India-based officer's equity creates perquisite TDS at vest and Schedule FA reporting.
countries.tw: Taiwan leaders are LSA-covered unless they are genuine mandated managers appointed under the Company Act, which changes severance and termination design. Include Taiwan pay (including year-end bonus and profit-sharing months) in the pay-ratio measure consistently.
countries.cn: China employees are in the pay-ratio population unless a documented privacy-law exclusion or de minimis exclusion applies; moving employee-level pay data to the US requires PIPL notice, separate consent and a cross-border transfer mechanism, so consider local aggregation. Any China-based officer's equity must be covered by the SAFE Circular 7 registration.

processes.name: Equity grant administration
processes.summary: End-to-end administration of new-hire, promotion, refresh and retention grants under the stock plan and the Equity Grant Policy: grants on a fixed calendar, Comp Committee approval for officers and delegated approval for everyone else, award agreements with country appendices, securities and exchange-control checks, and SOX reconciliation to ASC 718 accounting. Good looks like every grant approved before its grant date, a clean three-way reconciliation each quarter, and no grant made in a country before its legal set-up is complete.
processes.owner: Stock Admin (process), Total Rewards (guidelines and requests), Legal (plan, securities and country feasibility), Finance (ASC 718), Comp Committee (approval and delegation)
processes.trigger: Accepted offer with equity (TA-04), promotion (PD-04), annual refresh (CO-02) or retention award (CO-05), batched to the next scheduled grant date
outputs: Approved grant list (committee resolution or delegate consent)
Awards recorded in the equity platform
Award agreements with country appendices and acceptance records
ASC 718 valuation and expense schedule
Three-way reconciliation (approved list, equity platform, accounting)
Form 4 and country filings (e.g., SAFE Circular 7 updates)
processes.sla: Grants made on the first scheduled grant date after start or approval; recorded within 1 business day; Form 4 within 2 business days; agreements accepted within 90 days

steps.label: Compile grant requests by cutoff
steps.detail: Collect new-hire grants from accepted Greenhouse offers, promotion grants, annual refresh and retention grants into the batch for the next scheduled grant date (cutoff typically 10 business days before; new hires must have started). Value-based awards are converted to shares using the policy's averaging method (e.g., 30-trading-day average price).

steps.label: Validate against guidelines and pool
steps.detail: Check each request against level guidelines, approved exceptions, per-person plan limits, the available share reserve and the annual burn-rate budget. Confirm award type: RSUs globally, ISOs only for US employees within the $100,000 first-exercisable limit, PSUs only as the committee approved.
steps.control: Share reserve and burn-rate check before approval

steps.label: Confirm country and securities feasibility
steps.detail: Confirm the grant can be made in the employee's country: securities-law exemption for the offer, exchange control (China SAFE Circular 7 registration must cover the grantee before participation), data-privacy consent wording, and whether a cash-settled alternative is needed. A country matrix keeps routine grants from needing case-by-case review.

steps.label: Confirm grant date and MNPI timing
steps.detail: Confirm the batch is on the committee-approved grant calendar and that Legal has no MNPI hold in place (e.g., a pending major design win, acquisition or earnings surprise). Flag any NEO option falling from four business days before to one business day after a 10-Q, 10-K or MNPI 8-K for Item 402(x).
steps.control: 402(x)/MNPI timing checklist signed by Legal

steps.label: Officer grant or above delegation?
steps.detail: Grants to Section 16 officers and directors, and any grant above the per-employee or aggregate limits in the committee's written delegation, go to the Comp Committee; all others go to the delegate.

steps.label: Approve officer and large grants
steps.detail: The committee of non-employee directors (Rule 16b-3) approves grants at a meeting or by unanimous written consent effective on or before the grant date. Approvals are never retroactive; if approval slips, the grant moves to the next scheduled date.
steps.control: Signed resolution dated on or before the grant date

steps.label: Approve non-officer grants (delegated)
steps.detail: The CEO or equity award committee approves the non-officer list under the Comp Committee's written delegation (share and value caps, no grants to the delegate or to officers) by signed consent dated on or before the grant date. Delegated grants are reported to the committee each quarter.
steps.control: Delegation limits checked; signed delegate consent

steps.label: Record awards in equity platform
steps.detail: Enter each award from the signed approved list only: grant date, type, shares, vesting schedule, exercise price (closing price on the grant date for options), country and tax status. A second Stock Admin reviewer checks every record before release.

steps.label: File Form 4 and country filings
steps.detail: File Forms 4 for officer and director grants within two business days of the grant date, update the China SAFE Circular 7 registration for new participants through the WFOE agent, and confirm the Form S-8 reserve covers the shares. Other country filings follow the country matrix.

steps.label: Value and expense under ASC 718
steps.detail: Finance sets grant-date fair value (RSUs at grant-date price adjusted for dividends, options by Black-Scholes, TSR-based PSUs by Monte Carlo), applies the forfeiture policy and books expense from the equity platform's expense report.

steps.label: Reconcile approved list, platform, GL
steps.detail: Stock Admin and Finance reconcile the approved grant list, the equity platform and ASC 718 expense and cap table for every grant date and at quarter-end; exceptions are cleared before the quarterly close.
steps.control: SOX key control: approved grant list = equity platform = accounting, signed and retained

steps.label: Release agreements and appendices
steps.detail: Publish the award agreement with the relevant country appendix (tax, exchange control, securities, data privacy and, for Canada, termination wording that excludes the common-law notice period) on the equity platform and notify the grantee.

steps.label: Review and accept award agreement
steps.detail: The grantee reviews and electronically accepts the agreement, which records proof of acceptance (important in Canada) and any required PIPL or other consents.

steps.label: Accepted by deadline?
steps.detail: Acceptance is tracked against the policy deadline (e.g., 90 days or before the first vest). Non-acceptance is escalated through the manager; plan terms decide whether the award is forfeited or deemed accepted.

steps.label: Hand off to vesting administration
steps.detail: The award is live and handed to EQ-02 for vesting, release and tax withholding; grant records and approvals are archived.

controls.control: Grants made only on fixed calendar dates, with approval dated on or before the grant date (no backdating)
controls.evidence: Grant calendar, signed resolutions and delegate consents

controls.control: Three-way reconciliation of approved list, equity platform and ASC 718 expense
controls.evidence: Signed reconciliation per grant date and quarter-end

controls.control: Item 402(x) and MNPI timing check before each grant date
controls.evidence: Legal-signed timing checklist

controls.control: Delegated approvals within share and value caps; no delegate grants to officers or to the delegate
controls.evidence: Delegation resolution and exception log

controls.control: Country feasibility and exchange-control registration complete before participation (e.g., China SAFE)
controls.evidence: Country matrix and SAFE filing receipts

controls.control: Equity platform access reviewed quarterly; recorder and approver roles separated; SOC 1 Type II report reviewed
controls.evidence: Access review sign-off and SOC 1 bridge review

controls.control: Share reserve and burn rate monitored against plan limits and the committee's budget
controls.evidence: Quarterly share reserve report to the committee

kpis.name: Reconciliation exceptions
kpis.target: 0 open exceptions at quarter-end
kpis.why: Unreconciled grants are a SOX deficiency and misstate expense

kpis.name: Recording timeliness
kpis.target: 100% of grants recorded within 1 business day of the grant date
kpis.why: Late records delay Form 4s and agreements

kpis.name: Acceptance rate
kpis.target: >= 98% accepted within 90 days
kpis.why: Unaccepted terms weaken enforceability (notably in Canada)

kpis.name: Form 4 timeliness
kpis.target: 100% within 2 business days
kpis.why: Late filings are publicly disclosed under Item 405

kpis.name: Burn rate
kpis.target: Within the committee-approved annual budget
kpis.why: Overspending the pool forces an early share request to shareholders

considerations: Convert value-based guidelines to shares with a trailing average price to reduce volatility, and make offer letters say the value is approximate and shares are set at grant.
Use a fixed calendar (e.g., monthly for new hires, annual for refresh) inside open windows; fixed dates are the best defense against spring-loading or backdating allegations.
Put delegation in writing with share and value caps and no officer grants; grants to Section 16 officers need committee approval to keep the Rule 16b-3 exemption.
Limit ISOs to US employees and watch the $100,000 limit; RSUs are simpler for a global workforce.
Country appendices carry real legal weight: PIPL consent for China, exchange-control and tax notices, and Canadian termination wording that excludes the notice period.
