MNPI in a chip company often sits in engineering (tape-out results, major design wins); Legal needs a way to hear about it before a grant date.
Share reserve increases need shareholder approval (Nasdaq 5635(c)) and a current S-8; model burn rate and overhang against proxy-advisor scorecards a year ahead.
In 2027 very large grants to non-officer engineers can put them in the expanded 162(m) group, so flag outsized awards to Tax.

variations.when: Inducement grant to a new executive
variations.how: Granted under Nasdaq 5635(c)(4) with independent-director or committee approval and a press release announcing material terms; usually from a separate inducement plan.
Committee approval, Form 4 within two business days, and Item 402(x) timing check for options.
SAFE Circular 7 registration must cover the grantee before participation; proceeds flow through the special FX account.
Agreement wording excludes the common-law notice period and acceptance is recorded; track the C$200,000 stock-option deduction limit.

variations.when: Country where offering is not feasible
variations.how: Grant cash-settled RSUs or a cash retention award with equivalent vesting after Legal review.

variations.when: Acquisition with assumed or substitute awards
variations.how: Convert awards at the deal ratio under the assumed plan and reconcile the converted population separately.

variations.when: Grantee on leave at the grant date
variations.how: Grant proceeds if approved; vesting follows the plan's leave rules (EQ-02).

countries.us: ISOs may go only to employees, with only the first $100,000 (grant-date FMV) becoming exercisable each year qualifying and a 10-year maximum term; options must be priced at least at grant-date FMV (also a 409A condition for NSOs). Officer grants need Rule 16b-3-compliant committee approval and a Form 4 within two business days, and NEO option timing near MNPI is disclosed under Item 402(x).
countries.us-ca: From 2026 stock and options count as wages under the California Equal Pay Act (SB 642), so apply grant guidelines and exceptions consistently across comparable roles and document the reasons. Forfeiture of unvested equity on departure is generally allowed, but repayment of vested or paid amounts at departure may be caught by AB 692 and needs counsel review.
countries.ca: Award terms must clearly and unambiguously exclude the common-law notice period from vesting on termination (Matthews v. Ocean Nutrition, 2020 SCC 26), and the company must be able to prove the employee accepted the terms (Battiston v. Microsoft, 2021 ONCA 727). RSUs are taxed at vesting, and the 50% stock-option deduction is capped at C$200,000 of annual vesting value for large non-CCPC employers.
countries.in: RSUs and options create a salary perquisite at vest or exercise (FMV minus price paid) that the Indian entity must withhold through payroll (TDS under s.392, Income-tax Act 2025) and report on Form 123. Employees must report foreign shares in Schedule FA, and the recharge arrangement with the US parent affects deductibility and transfer pricing.
countries.tw: US-parent RSUs are a key differentiator against TSMC and MediaTek cash profit-sharing, so present grant value in total-compensation terms. Confirm Taiwan tax treatment of vesting income, NHI obligations and any securities or FX filing for offering parent shares with local advisors before first grants (verify).
countries.cn: The plan must be registered with SAFE under Circular 7 through a domestic agent (usually the WFOE) before PRC employees participate, with change registrations, quarterly filings and a special FX account for proceeds. The WFOE withholds IIT at vest or exercise (listed-company equity income can be taxed separately through 31 Dec 2027), and sending grantee data to the US equity platform needs PIPL notice and separate consent.

processes.name: Vesting, release & tax withholding
processes.summary: Processes each RSU/PSU vest and option exercise: confirm employment and leave status, calculate taxable income, fund taxes by sell-to-cover or net settlement, report income and remit tax through each country's payroll, and deliver shares to the broker. Good looks like zero releases to terminated employees, payroll reporting within one business day in every country and withholding that reconciles to the equity platform.
processes.owner: Stock Admin (release process), Payroll (income reporting and tax remittance), Tax (withholding rules), Legal (insider rules for sales)
processes.trigger: A scheduled RSU/PSU vest date or an option exercise request
outputs: Pre-vest status exception report
Release report with taxable income by country
Sell-to-cover or share-withholding record
Payroll equity income import files by country
Release-to-payroll-to-GL reconciliation
Year-end equity income reporting (W-2, T4, Form 130/123, Taiwan and China filings)
processes.sla: Equity income to each country payroll within 1 business day of vest; taxes remitted by local deadlines; shares in brokerage accounts within 3 business days

steps.label: Run pre-vest status check
steps.detail: Five business days before each vest date, compare the equity platform with Darwinbox for terminations, leaves of absence, transfers and deaths so vesting is stopped, suspended or accelerated under plan terms.

steps.label: Confirm exits, leaves and moves
steps.detail: People Ops confirms termination dates, leave types and dates, and cross-border moves with workday data for tax sourcing (MV-02), and corrects Darwinbox before the vest.
steps.control: Pre-vest exception report cleared and signed

steps.label: Apply blackout and 10b5-1 rules
steps.detail: Sell-to-cover under a non-discretionary instruction or a 10b5-1-compliant election may proceed during a blackout (the overlapping-plan exception covers sell-to-cover), while discretionary sales wait for an open window. Section 16 officers' share withholding is reported on Form 4 (EQ-05).

steps.label: Sell-to-cover or net settle?
steps.detail: The plan and country matrix decide the method: sell-to-cover is the default for most employees; net settlement is used for Section 16 officers or where market sales are impractical.

steps.label: Instruct broker sell-to-cover
steps.detail: The broker sells enough shares to cover estimated tax and fees and remits proceeds to the employing entity so local payroll can deposit the tax.

steps.label: Withhold shares; company funds tax
steps.detail: The company withholds shares up to the maximum statutory rate (to keep equity accounting treatment) and funds the tax in cash from the employing entity; Treasury is told the cash need in advance.

steps.label: Report income and remit taxes
steps.detail: Each country payroll loads equity income and tax withheld, applies local rules (US supplemental rates, Canada T4 codes, India perquisite TDS, Taiwan and China individual income tax), remits tax and trues up over- or under-withholding in the next payroll.

steps.label: Receive shares and statements
steps.detail: Shares land in the employee's brokerage account with a release confirmation. Any later sale follows the insider trading policy and local reporting (e.g., India Schedule FA, China FX repatriation).

steps.label: Reconcile release to payroll and GL
steps.detail: Reconcile the release report, payroll imports and GL entries by country for each vest cycle and clear differences before month-end close.
steps.control: Release report = payroll import = GL, reviewed by Finance

controls.control: Pre-vest reconciliation of equity platform status against HRIS terminations, leaves and transfers
controls.evidence: Signed exception report per vest date

controls.control: Release report reconciled to payroll imports and GL by country
controls.evidence: Reconciliation with Finance review

controls.control: Withholding rates and country matrix reviewed by Tax each year and on law changes
controls.evidence: Tax sign-off on platform rate tables

kpis.name: Erroneous releases
kpis.target: 0 releases to terminated employees
kpis.why: Recovering shares from leavers is slow and often impossible across borders

kpis.name: Payroll reporting timeliness
kpis.target: 100% of vest events reported to payroll within 1 business day
kpis.why: Late reporting causes late tax deposits and penalties

kpis.name: Withholding accuracy
kpis.target: < 1% of events need a true-up beyond rounding
kpis.why: True-ups create employee confusion and extra payroll work

considerations: Sell-to-cover saves company cash but puts shares on the market; net settlement conserves the share reserve but uses cash. Choose by population and revisit when the stock price or share reserve changes.
Structure standing sell-to-cover elections to fit the Rule 10b5-1 overlapping-plan exception, or releases during blackouts become a problem for insiders.

Leave-of-absence vesting rules (e.g., suspension after 6 months of unpaid leave) must be written in the plan and applied only where local law permits; protected leave such as CFRA/FMLA, Taiwan parental leave or China maternity leave needs Legal review before tolling.
Mobile employees create multi-state and multi-country tax sourcing; capture workday location at the time of the move, not at vest.

variations.how: FICA is due when the award is no longer subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture (at retirement eligibility), not at settlement, so Payroll reports FICA separately (verify plan terms).
Apply plan acceleration and release to the estate or beneficiary with OF-09; tax reporting follows local rules.

variations.when: Termination on or near the vest date
variations.how: Vesting stops on the termination date per plan; Canadian awards follow the agreement's notice-period wording.

countries.us: Federal supplemental withholding is 22%, with a mandatory 37% on supplemental wages over $1M in a year, and Social Security applies up to the $184,500 wage base (2026). Officers report withheld shares on Form 4 within two business days.
countries.us-ca: Withhold California income tax at the supplemental rate for stock and bonus income (10.23%, verify) and SDI at 1.3% on all wages with no wage cap (2026), which applies in full to RSU income.
countries.ca: RSUs are employment income at vesting and options are taxed at exercise; withhold income tax, CPP/CPP2 and EI up to annual maximums and report on the T4 with the correct codes.
countries.in: The perquisite (FMV at vest or exercise minus price paid) is taxed as salary with TDS through Indian payroll under s.392 of the Income-tax Act 2025 and reported on Form 123 and Form 130; remind employees to disclose foreign shares in Schedule FA.
countries.tw: Vesting income is taxable for Taiwan individual income tax and may attract the NHI supplementary premium; confirm withholding versus self-reporting treatment with tax advisors (verify).
countries.cn: The WFOE withholds IIT at vest or exercise as wages, with listed-company equity income taxable separately from other wages through 31 Dec 2027, and sale proceeds must be repatriated through the SAFE-registered special FX account.

processes.name: ESPP enrollment & purchase
processes.summary: Runs the Employee Stock Purchase Plan: an IRC 423 component for US employees and a non-423 component for participating non-US entities. Covers offering periods, enrollment, payroll contributions in local currency, discounted purchases, the $25,000 limit, share delivery, disposition tracking and Form 3922. Good looks like high participation, contributions that reconcile to purchases in every country, and no country launched before exchange-control and securities checks.
processes.owner: Stock Admin (plan administration), Payroll (contributions and refunds), Total Rewards (plan design), Legal (country feasibility and securities)
processes.trigger: Offering-period enrollment window (e.g., every six months) and each purchase date
outputs: Offering terms and participating-country list
Enrollment elections and payroll deduction authorizations
Contribution reports by country with FX conversion record
Purchase report and broker share deposit
Refunds of excess or leavers' contributions
Forms 3922 and disqualifying-disposition income reporting
processes.sla: Enrollment opens 2-3 weeks before each offering; contributions transmitted within 3 business days of the purchase date; Forms 3922 by January 31

steps.label: Confirm offering terms
steps.detail: Confirm offering and purchase periods (e.g., 24-month offering with four 6-month purchases and a reset if the price falls), 15% discount with lookback, eligibility exclusions, contribution limits and remaining share reserve.

steps.label: Confirm non-US participation
steps.detail: Confirm each participating entity: Canada (non-423 component, taxable discount), India (FEMA ODI/LRS), Taiwan (securities and FX filings, verify) and China (SAFE Circular 7 registration covering the ESPP before any contributions are remitted).

steps.label: Open enrollment window
steps.detail: Send the eligibility file from Darwinbox to the equity platform, publish translated materials and open enrollment; designated insiders may enroll or change elections only in an open trading window.
steps.control: Eligibility file reconciled to Darwinbox before enrollment opens

steps.label: Enroll and elect contribution %
steps.detail: Eligible employees elect a contribution rate (e.g., 1-15% of eligible pay) and accept plan terms and data-privacy consents, which also serve as the written payroll deduction authorization.

steps.label: Deduct contributions each payroll
steps.detail: Each country payroll deducts contributions in local currency and holds them in the employing entity; deductions stop on termination or withdrawal.

steps.label: Limits exceeded?
steps.detail: Before purchase, the platform tests the $25,000 annual accrual limit (423 component) and per-period share caps.

steps.label: Refund excess contributions
steps.detail: Payroll refunds excess contributions to the employee in the next payroll cycle.

steps.label: Purchase and deposit shares
steps.detail: Purchase at 85% of the lower of the offering-date and purchase-date price, convert non-US contributions at the documented FX rate, deposit shares with the broker and send purchase data to country payrolls and Legal.
steps.control: Contributions per payroll register = funds transmitted = shares purchased x price, by country

steps.label: Track dispositions; issue 3922
steps.detail: Track qualifying and disqualifying dispositions for W-2 reporting, issue Forms 3922 by January 31, and provide non-US tax reporting data.

controls.control: Eligibility file reconciled to Darwinbox before each enrollment
controls.evidence: Reconciliation report

controls.control: Contributions reconciled to funds transmitted and shares purchased, by country
controls.evidence: Purchase reconciliation with reviewer sign-off

controls.control: $25,000 accrual limit and share caps enforced in the platform before purchase
controls.evidence: Limit test report and refund log

kpis.name: Participation
kpis.target: >= 50% of eligible employees
kpis.why: Low participation means the plan's cost is not buying engagement

kpis.name: Purchase reconciliation
kpis.target: 100% of countries reconciled each purchase date
kpis.why: Unreconciled contributions are an audit finding and employee money at risk

kpis.name: Form 3922 timeliness
kpis.target: 100% furnished by January 31
kpis.why: Late forms bring IRS penalties and employee complaints

considerations: The lookback and reset features make the plan valuable but raise ASC 718 expense; model cost before changing offering terms.
Non-US participation is where the risk sits: China needs SAFE registration before contributions leave the country and India's FEMA rules apply, so launch a country only after Legal signs off.
Decide who bears FX risk on accumulated non-US contributions and say so in plan materials.
Plan rules must say when contributions stop on leave; under 423 rules a leave longer than 3 months ends the employment relationship unless reemployment is guaranteed by statute or contract.

variations.how: Automatic withdrawal and refund of accumulated contributions through payroll; no purchase.

variations.when: Transfer between participating entities or countries
variations.how: Continue in the offering where plan terms allow, switching payroll and deduction currency; 423 status depends on the new employer's participation.
Complete the Legal feasibility checklist, translate materials, and set up payroll deduction and remittance before the next enrollment.

countries.us: IRC 423 requires shareholder approval within 12 months, broad eligibility (permitted exclusions: under 2 years' service, 20 hours/week or less, 5 months/year or less, highly compensated employees), a price of at least 85% of FMV, a $25,000 annual accrual limit and offering periods up to 27 months; furnish Form 3922 by January 31.
countries.us-ca: Payroll deductions need the employee's written authorization (LC 224), which the enrollment election provides; refund accumulated contributions promptly after termination in line with final-pay timing (verify).
countries.ca: Canadian employees participate through the non-423 component; the purchase discount is taxable employment income reported on the T4.
countries.in: ESPP purchases by resident employees fall under FEMA ODI/LRS rules, the discount is a salary perquisite with TDS through Indian payroll, and employees must report the shares in Schedule FA.
countries.tw: Before enrolling Taiwan employees, confirm with local counsel any securities filing for offering parent shares, FX reporting for remitting contributions and the tax treatment of the discount (verify).
countries.cn: ESPP payroll contributions cannot be remitted abroad without SAFE Circular 7 registration, and the WFOE withholds IIT on the discount (listed-company equity income taxed separately through 31 Dec 2027).

processes.name: Insider trading pre-clearance & blackouts
processes.summary: Prevents insider trading by maintaining designated insider lists, running quarterly trading windows and event-specific blackouts, pre-clearing trades and reviewing Rule 10b5-1 plans, and captures the data needed for Item 408 disclosure. In a chip company MNPI often sits with engineers and sales staff (design wins, tape-out results, customer forecasts), not just Finance. Good looks like accurate lists, one-day pre-clearance, broker-enforced blocks and zero violations.
processes.owner: Legal (Securities) - insider trading compliance officer, Stock Admin (broker controls), People Ops (list feeds and acknowledgments)
processes.trigger: Quarterly calendar; a project that creates MNPI (major design win, M&A, material customer event); a pre-clearance or 10b5-1 plan request
outputs: Designated insider and project-specific lists
Blackout and open-window notices
Pre-clearance decision log
Rule 10b5-1 plan register with cooling-off end dates
Item 408(a) data for officers and directors
Policy acknowledgments and annual certifications
processes.sla: Pre-clearance decision within 1 business day; approvals valid for 2 trading days inside an open window

steps.label: Maintain designated insider lists
steps.detail: Each quarter Legal refreshes the lists: directors, officers, finance and legal staff, plus role-based insiders such as program managers, design leads who see tape-out results and sales staff with customer forecasts or design-win news. Project lists are opened for deals or material customer events.

steps.label: Feed hires, moves and exits
steps.detail: Darwinbox triggers notify Legal of hires, role changes and exits in listed roles, and People Ops collects policy acknowledgments at onboarding through the LMS.
steps.control: Quarterly reconciliation of insider lists to Darwinbox roles

steps.label: Issue window and blackout notices
steps.detail: Send quarterly blackout notices (typically starting about two weeks before quarter-end until results are public) and confidential event-specific blackouts to project lists without stating the reason.

steps.label: Apply broker trading blocks
steps.detail: Set broker and equity platform restrictions so designated insiders cannot sell without a pre-clearance code in open windows, or at all during blackouts.
steps.control: Broker-enforced blocks for designated insiders

steps.label: Request pre-clearance or 10b5-1 plan
steps.detail: Designated insiders submit trade requests (including gifts) or proposed 10b5-1 plans and certify they hold no MNPI; plans may be adopted only in an open window.

steps.label: Approve request?
steps.detail: Legal checks window status, list membership, MNPI in live projects, Section 16(b) matchable trades and 10b5-1 conditions.

steps.label: Log approval; track cooling-off
steps.detail: Log the approval and its validity. For 10b5-1 plans record the cooling-off end (officers and directors: later of 90 days or 2 business days after the 10-Q/10-K, maximum 120 days; others 30 days), check for overlapping or repeat single-trade plans, and capture officer and director adoptions for Item 408(a).
steps.control: 10b5-1 plan checklist and register

steps.label: Trade within approved window
steps.detail: The insider trades within the approval validity; brokers of Section 16 insiders notify Legal the same day for Form 4.

steps.label: Denied; no trade
steps.detail: The insider is told the request is denied without the reason and must not trade or tip others.

controls.control: Designated insiders can trade only with a pre-clearance code, enforced at the broker
controls.evidence: Pre-clearance log and broker restriction reports

controls.control: Insider lists reconciled quarterly to Darwinbox roles and the Section 16 list
controls.evidence: Signed quarterly reconciliation

controls.control: 10b5-1 plans reviewed for cooling-off, overlap and single-trade limits before adoption
controls.evidence: Completed plan checklist and register

kpis.name: Pre-clearance turnaround
kpis.target: >= 95% decided within 1 business day
kpis.why: Slow decisions push insiders to trade around the process

kpis.name: List accuracy
kpis.target: 0 missed role changes at quarterly reconciliation
kpis.why: An insider missing from the list is not blocked at the broker

kpis.name: Certification completion
kpis.target: 100% of designated insiders certify annually
kpis.why: Evidence that insiders know and accept the policy

kpis.name: Violations
kpis.target: 0 trades outside policy
kpis.why: Outcome measure of the whole control set

considerations: Build lists by role and project, not title: in a chip company the people who know about a socket win or a failed tape-out are engineers and FAEs.
Cover shadow trading in policy and training: the SEC v. Panuwat verdict (2024) supports liability for trading a customer's, supplier's or competitor's stock on company MNPI.
Keep event-specific blackouts confidential; the notice itself can be MNPI.
If the proposed optional semiannual reporting (Form 10-S) is adopted and elected, windows and 10b5-1 cooling-off periods keyed to 10-Q filings must be redesigned.
Translate policy and training for Taiwan, China and India staff and collect local-language acknowledgments.

variations.how: Pre-clear every transaction including gifts; broker notifies Legal the same day; Form 4 within two business days (EQ-05).
The policy continues to apply until the information is public or stale; exit reminders are given in OF-01.
Treated as termination and adoption of a new plan with a new cooling-off period.

countries.us: The policy is filed as Form 10-K Exhibit 19, officer and director 10b5-1 adoptions and terminations are disclosed quarterly under Item 408(a), and hedging policy is disclosed under Item 407(i).
countries.us-ca: No material variation from global standard; make sure the policy's confidentiality wording does not restrict discussing wages or reporting to regulators.
countries.ca: No material variation from global standard for trading parent shares on Nasdaq; confirm with counsel whether Canadian securities rules reach trading in Canadian-listed customers or suppliers on company MNPI (verify).
countries.in: Resident employees hold parent shares under FEMA ODI rules and report them in Schedule FA; trading Indian-listed customers' or suppliers' shares on company MNPI may also breach SEBI insider trading rules (verify).
countries.tw: Provide the policy in Traditional Chinese; trading Taiwan-listed foundry, packaging or customer shares on company MNPI may breach Securities and Exchange Act insider trading provisions (verify).
countries.cn: Provide the policy in Chinese with signed acknowledgment; employees trade parent shares only through the SAFE-registered plan broker, and trading A-share partners on company MNPI may breach the PRC Securities Law (verify).

processes.name: Section 16 reporting
processes.summary: Files Section 16(a) reports (Forms 3, 4 and 5) for directors and Section 16 officers on time under EDGAR Next, supported by powers of attorney, broker pre-clearance and same-day data feeds from HR, Stock Admin and brokers. Good looks like zero late filings disclosed under Item 405 and current EDGAR access for every insider.
processes.owner: Legal (Securities) / Corporate Secretary (filings), Stock Admin (transaction data), People Ops (officer status changes)
processes.trigger: Appointment or promotion into Section 16 status; any reportable transaction (grant, share withholding, exercise, open-market trade, gift, 10b5-1 trade); fiscal year-end
outputs: Section 16 officer and director list
EDGAR Next credentials, account administrators and delegations
Signed powers of attorney
Filed Forms 3, 4 and 5 with confirmations
Transaction tracker and late-filing log for Item 405
Year-end holdings reconciliation for the proxy ownership table
processes.sla: Form 3 within 10 days of becoming an insider; Form 4 within 2 business days; Form 5 within 45 days after fiscal year-end

steps.label: Notify Legal of officer change
steps.detail: People Ops notifies Legal the same day a person is appointed or promoted into a Rule 16a-1(f) officer role, a director joins, or an insider leaves.
steps.control: Same-day notification log

steps.label: Set up EDGAR Next access and POA
steps.detail: Legal arranges the insider's individual Login.gov-based EDGAR Next credentials, account administrators and delegation to the company filer, obtains a signed power of attorney, and briefs the insider on Section 16(b), Rule 144 and pre-clearance.

steps.label: File Form 3 within 10 days
steps.detail: File the initial holdings report within 10 days of becoming an insider, using equity platform and broker data confirmed by the insider.

steps.label: Pre-clear every transaction
steps.detail: The insider pre-clears all transactions, including gifts, and instructs brokers to notify Legal the same day of any execution, including 10b5-1 trades.

steps.label: Send transaction data in 1 bd
steps.detail: Stock Admin sends grants, share withholding (code F), exercises and ESPP data to Legal within one business day; brokers send open-market trade confirmations.

steps.label: Prepare and file Form 4
steps.detail: Prepare the Form 4 with the right transaction codes and, where relevant, the 10b5-1 checkbox and plan adoption date; confirm with the insider and file within two business days.
steps.control: Filing tracker with due date and filed timestamp per transaction

steps.label: Filed on time and accurate?
steps.detail: Legal compares the filed time to the deadline and checks reported holdings against the equity platform.

steps.label: Amend and log for Item 405
steps.detail: File any amendment, log the late filing for proxy disclosure under Item 405, and fix the root cause (data feed, broker notice or access).

steps.label: Form 5 and year-end reconciliation
steps.detail: Within 45 days after fiscal year-end, file any Forms 5 and reconcile each insider's reported holdings to equity platform and broker statements for the proxy ownership table.

raci.activity: EDGAR access and powers of attorney

controls.control: Same-day HR notice to Legal of Section 16 status changes
controls.evidence: Notification log matched to Form 3 dates

controls.control: Transaction feeds from the equity platform and brokers tracked to filing deadlines
controls.evidence: Filing tracker

controls.control: Year-end reconciliation of reported holdings to equity platform and broker statements
controls.evidence: Signed reconciliation per insider

kpis.name: Form 4 timeliness
kpis.target: 100% within 2 business days
kpis.why: Late filings are disclosed in the proxy and can draw SEC enforcement

kpis.name: Item 405 delinquencies
kpis.target: 0 per year
kpis.why: Public signal of weak controls

kpis.name: EDGAR access currency
kpis.target: 100% of insiders with working credentials and delegations
kpis.why: Missing access is the most common cause of late filings under EDGAR Next

considerations: Most late Forms 4 come from share withholding at vest and gifts; automate the equity platform feed and remind insiders that bona fide gifts have been Form 4 items since 2023.
Check Section 16(b) matchable transactions at pre-clearance; any purchase and sale within six months can lead to strict-liability disgorgement demands from firms that monitor Forms 4.
EDGAR Next makes access individual; keep at least two account administrators so departures or lost credentials do not stop filings.
Coordinate Form 144 for affiliate sales over 5,000 shares or $50,000 in three months with the Form 4.

variations.when: New director or officer hired from outside
variations.how: Start EDGAR Next setup before the start date; Form 3 within 10 days; inducement grants reported on Form 4.
Update the officer list; transactions after departure may still be reportable if matched with pre-departure transactions within six months (verify).
Deadlines run on US business days; set up credentials and broker notice channels in advance for Taiwan, China or India time zones.

countries.us: Rules 16a-1 to 16a-13 apply: Form 3 within 10 days, Form 4 within two business days (including bona fide gifts since 2023) and Form 5 within 45 days after fiscal year-end; EDGAR Next, mandatory since Sept 2025, requires individual Login.gov credentials and delegations.
countries.us-ca: No material variation from global standard.
countries.ca: No material variation from global standard for Nasdaq reporting; Canadian insider reporting would apply only if the company became a Canadian reporting issuer (verify).
countries.in: No material variation from global standard; shares withheld for an India-based officer's TDS at vest are still reported on Form 4 (code F).
countries.tw: No material variation from global standard; plan around time zones because the two-business-day clock runs on US business days.
countries.cn: No material variation in US reporting; a China-based officer's sale proceeds must also flow through the SAFE Circular 7 special FX account.

processes.name: Clawback administration
processes.summary: Administers the Compensation Recovery Policy: keeps the executive officer register and incentive calculation records, and when an accounting restatement is required, identifies, calculates (pre-tax), recovers and discloses erroneously awarded incentive compensation. Also runs discretionary misconduct clawbacks where the policy provides them. Good looks like records ready for any three-year lookback, no indemnification, and recovery methods that work under each country's wage-deduction limits.
processes.owner: Comp Committee (policy administrator), Legal (determination and recovery), Total Rewards (calculation), Finance (restatement and financial measures)
processes.trigger: The date the board, audit committee or authorized officers conclude (or reasonably should have concluded) that an accounting restatement is required, Big R or little r; or a misconduct finding under discretionary provisions
outputs: Trigger memo with restatement date and lookback years
Covered executive and award list
Pre-tax recovery calculation with TSR/stock-price methodology
Comp Committee resolution and any impracticability determination
Demand letters, repayment agreements or award cancellations
Item 402(w) disclosure and 10-K cover checkbox support
processes.sla: Recovery calculation within 60 days of the restatement determination; recovery completed reasonably promptly (target 90 days)

steps.label: Determine restatement is required
steps.detail: Finance and the audit committee document the date a restatement to correct a material error (Big R), or an error that would be material if left uncorrected (little r), was or should have been determined; that date fixes the three completed fiscal years in the lookback.

steps.label: Identify covered executives and awards
steps.detail: List current and former executive officers (Rule 16a-1(f)) and all incentive compensation they received in the lookback that was based wholly or partly on a financial reporting measure, including stock price and TSR; compensation is 'received' when the measure is attained.

steps.label: Recalculate erroneous amounts
steps.detail: Recompute each award on restated results, pre-tax; for stock-price or TSR awards use the reasonable-estimate method pre-agreed with the compensation consultant and document it.
steps.control: Independent Finance and consultant review of each calculation

steps.label: Approve recovery amounts
steps.detail: The committee approves the amounts owed; its only discretion is the narrow impracticability exceptions.

steps.label: Impracticability exception applies?
steps.detail: Exceptions are limited: enforcement cost exceeds the amount after a documented reasonable attempt, recovery would violate home-country law adopted before Nov 28, 2022 (with a legal opinion), or it would disqualify a tax-qualified retirement plan.

steps.label: Issue recovery demand
steps.detail: Send a demand stating the amount and method: direct repayment, cancellation of unvested or unpaid awards, offset against future incentive pay (subject to 409A) or forfeiture of deferred compensation. Confirm no indemnification, insurance or separation-agreement term covers the amount.
steps.control: Legal check that no indemnification, D&O coverage or gross-up applies

steps.label: Apply offsets within local limits
steps.detail: Where offset is used, Payroll applies it only within local deduction rules and with any required written authorization; otherwise it records repayments received.

steps.label: Repay or sign repayment plan
steps.detail: The executive repays or signs a repayment agreement; unpaid amounts go to Legal for enforcement.

steps.label: Disclose under Item 402(w)
steps.detail: Disclose the recovery analysis under Item 402(w), including amounts outstanding 180 days or more, check the 10-K cover-page boxes and keep Exhibit 97 current.

controls.control: Executive officer register maintained, acknowledgments signed and incentive calculations kept for at least three years
controls.evidence: Register, signed acknowledgments and calculation archive

controls.control: No indemnification, insurance or gross-up covers recovered amounts
controls.evidence: Legal review of separation agreements, indemnity terms and D&O policy

controls.control: Recovery calculations independently reviewed before committee approval
controls.evidence: Finance and consultant review memo

controls.control: Annual check that Exhibit 97, 10-K cover checkboxes and award documents reference the current policy
controls.evidence: Annual Legal checklist

kpis.name: Acknowledgments
kpis.target: 100% of executive officers signed within 30 days of appointment
kpis.why: Signed terms make recovery enforceable across countries

kpis.name: Record readiness
kpis.target: 100% of incentive calculations retrievable for the last three fiscal years
kpis.why: Recovery must be calculated years after the payout

kpis.name: Recovery completion
kpis.target: 100% recovered or documented as impracticable within 90 days
kpis.why: Nasdaq 5608 requires recovery reasonably promptly

considerations: Recovery is mandatory and no-fault: an executive who did nothing wrong still repays, so say this at appointment and in every award agreement.
Calculate pre-tax and do not gross up, indemnify or insure the loss, including through a release in a separation agreement.
Agree the TSR and stock-price estimation method before you need it; building it during a restatement looks results-driven.

Prefer recovery by cancelling unvested awards or direct repayment; payroll offsets run into wage-deduction limits in California, Canada, India, Taiwan and China and into 409A limits on deferred compensation.
Keep discretionary misconduct clawbacks (e.g., export-control or fraud violations) separate from the mandatory Rule 10D-1 policy; regulators credit pay clawbacks tied to compliance failures.

variations.how: No payroll offset: demand letter and repayment agreement, escalating to litigation if unpaid.
The committee acts under POL-06 for covered employees after a documented investigation (ER-02), within local law limits.
Use award cancellation and direct repayment, with local counsel advice on deduction limits and tax on amounts already taxed.

countries.us: Rule 10D-1 and Nasdaq 5608 require recovery, without regard to fault and reasonably promptly, of incentive compensation received by current and former executive officers in the three completed fiscal years before the restatement date, calculated pre-tax; the policy is filed as Exhibit 97, and failure to adopt, disclose or enforce it can lead to delisting.
countries.us-ca: Payroll offsets are limited to lawful, authorized deductions (LC 221, 224), and AB 692 restricts repayment demands at separation under agreements from 1 Jan 2026, so confirm with counsel how it interacts with the mandated policy (verify) and recover by cancellation or direct repayment.
countries.ca: Deductions from wages need written authorization and statutory permission in Ontario and BC, so recover by direct repayment or award cancellation, and have clawback terms acknowledged in writing with consideration.
countries.in: Deductions are limited to authorised items and capped at 50% of wages (Code on Wages s.18), so recover by repayment agreement or cancellation of unvested RSUs, with tax advice on perquisites already taxed (verify).
countries.tw: LSA Art. 26 bars pre-deduction of damages or penalties from wages, so recover through a separate repayment agreement or award cancellation, and confirm whether the executive is LSA-covered or a mandated manager.
countries.cn: Deductions for employee-caused losses are capped at 20% of monthly wage and cannot take pay below minimum wage, so use repayment agreements or award cancellation backed by contract terms or rules adopted through democratic procedure.
